title: Mesh convergence and singularity discrimination
purpose: Determine whether a changing finite-element result reflects converging physical response, discretisation error, a geometric or loading singularity, or an unsuitable reported quantity.
engineering_questions: Which response quantity should converge for the stated engineering objective?
Is the observation point tied to a singular boundary, point load, sharp re-entrant corner, crack tip or incompatible constraint?
Do global energy and reaction quantities behave differently from local peaks?

evidence_requirements.name: mesh sequence
evidence_requirements.purpose: Compare the same model and response definition across controlled refinements.

procedure: Define the engineering response and reporting location before refining the mesh.
Refine in a controlled manner while preserving geometry, loads, constraints and output definitions.
Track local peaks, path or averaged quantities, reactions and energy measures separately.
Diagnose singular behaviour from trends rather than forcing a convergence declaration.
Record what can and cannot be interpreted from the current model.
tool_guidance: Generate the current mesh study code from the current geometry and solver model.
Retain all mesh and result metadata needed to reproduce each point.
non_goals: Forcing a fixed number of mesh levels
